glance: Stock futures edge higher after Monday's historic rally; Nvidia closed up 31.5% at $165.05 on Jensen Huang's return as CEO.
Reports say Trump brushed aside US intelligence findings to back Huang's reinstatement, citing the need to stop market losses.
OpenAI and Anthropic staff reportedly warn that internal, unreleased models have advanced too fast to release safely.
US probes whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers via a Fortinet router flaw.
Trump signals strikes on Iran could resume next year if talks fail, as Bahrain intercepts new Iranian attacks.

tech.headline: New details emerge on how Huang got his Nvidia job back
tech.summary: The New York Times reports President Trump set aside US intelligence findings in pushing for Jensen Huang's reinstatement, telling CNBC he needed to halt the market slide. The FT says a Silicon Valley group including Marc Andreessen and Brad Gerstner lobbied Trump and JD Vance, while the WSJ reports Huang disclosed additional affairs to the board on Sunday. The episode raises governance and conflict-of-interest questions even as investors cheered the outcome.

tech.headline: AI insiders warn unreleased models may be too risky to ship
tech.summary: Axios reports that employees at OpenAI and Anthropic say internal models have made rapid gains in reasoning, enough that they consider them unsafe for public release. The warnings come a day after OpenAI called for tougher government rules on frontier AI, adding pressure on regulators to act.

tech.headline: US investigates Iran over tanker cyberattacks
tech.summary: Investigators are looking at whether Iran used a Fortinet router vulnerability to hit as many as 50 energy tankers, according to the Wall Street Journal; Russia is also under consideration. If confirmed, it would mark a significant expansion of the Iran conflict into maritime and energy infrastructure. Organizations running Fortinet gear should check for patches.

tech.headline: Ex-OpenAI engineer allegedly recorded dozens of meetings
tech.summary: Prosecutors say the former OpenAI engineer charged with bugging an executive conference room had dozens of meeting recordings, many likely touching trade secrets. A filing also says he recorded a meeting with foreign government representatives. Separately, the FT reports AI labs are hiring ex-CIA staff and restricting employee movement to counter espionage.

tech.headline: Singapore vows it won't be a back door for Nvidia chips
tech.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore will not be used to get around US chip export controls as authorities investigate Megaspeed's purchases of Nvidia processors. The case highlights continued US scrutiny of AI chips flowing to China through third countries.

tech.headline: Meta launches its Muse AI agent in the UK
tech.summary: Meta rolled out Muse, a personal AI agent that handles everyday tasks, to adults in the UK. Politico says it is the first agent product from a Big Tech company launched there, a test case for how agents fare under UK rules.

tech.headline: OpenAI expands GPT-6.2 Sol and teams with Cisco on security tool
tech.summary: ChatGPT's Chat tab now offers a GPT-6.2 Sol version tuned for everyday conversation to paid Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users, and OpenAI set retirement dates for two older models. OpenAI and Cisco also released Shirudo, an open-source runtime that shields live Linux systems while patches are pending, without a reboot.

markets.summary: Futures are modestly higher after Monday's huge rebound (S&P 500 +4.7%, Nasdaq +6.5%, Dow +3%), with traders pricing a likely December Fed rate hike and eyeing Wednesday's PCE inflation data.

movers.name: Nvidia
movers.note: Monday close at $165.05 after Huang reinstated; best day since 2003

movers.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
movers.note: After hours: revenue beat, but outlook below top estimates

other.headline: Trump says Iran strikes could resume next year
other.summary: President Trump suggested US strikes on Iran may restart in the new year if negotiations fail, after rejecting Tehran's latest terms. The US is also weighing whether to delay action despite Israeli pressure.

other.headline: Bahrain intercepts Iranian attacks; Tehran readies tankers
other.summary: Bahrain said it intercepted new Iranian attacks, while Iran is reportedly preparing 14 oil tankers to try to break the US naval blockade, a possible flashpoint for oil prices.

other.headline: Markets now expect a December Fed rate hike
other.summary: CME FedWatch shows traders pricing roughly a 96% chance of a quarter-point increase next month. Wednesday's PCE inflation report is the next big test.

other.headline: About 81 million Americans expected to travel for Thanksgiving
other.summary: AAA forecasts more than 81 million travelers this week, slightly below last year's record, as high airfares and gas prices weigh on trips.

other.headline: Kalshi halts operations in Utah after court loss
other.summary: The prediction market paused service for more than 177,000 Utah users after losing a federal case over the state's gambling law, and it also faces criminal charges in the state.
